I've been farming this 1.5 mu plot for 20 years now — me and my wife handle most of the work, though my eldest son and daughter-in-law work in a factory in Handan and send money home. With six people in the household and only this little piece of land, I can't afford to mess up. We mainly grow for our own flour and grain, so a bad year means we have to buy from the market.

For the winter wheat, I'll plant around October 8th, after the National Day holiday when the soil is still warm. I'm using Jinmai 47 — I've grown it for three years and it does well in our village. I saved some seed from last year, but with only 1.5 mu I'll buy about 25 kg of fresh certified seed to make sure germination is good; that runs about 20 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, the extension agent said 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I don't mind putting a bit more to be safe on such a small plot. I'll spread 50 kg of compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 kind — as base fertilizer before planting, then topdress with 15 kg of urea when the wheat starts jointing in March. I know that's a little more than some neighbors use, but I'd rather waste a few yuan than risk the wheat turning yellow. I'll irrigate three times: the overwinter water in November, once at jointing in spring, and once at grain filling in May. Groundwater costs money, but I can't skip it — last year my cousin missed the jointing irrigation and his yield dropped by nearly 100 jin per mu. I'll spray herbicide once after emergence to kill the weeds; if I see aphids in spring I might add insecticide, but I'll decide when I see them.

For the summer maize, the turnaround is brutal — we harvest wheat in early June and I need to get the maize in the ground within two or three days. No time for deep plowing; I'll just shallow-till and plant. Everyone here uses Zhengdan 958 hybrid, and you can't save seed from hybrids anyway, so I'll buy fresh seed — about 2.5 kg per mu at roughly 30 yuan per mu. I'll put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer at planting, and if the plants look yellow at tasseling I'll throw on a little urea. Maize is more forgiving than wheat. I'll irrigate once or twice, usually once at the big trumpet stage if June and July are dry.

All in all, I'll spend around 500 yuan on inputs for the whole year. That's manageable with my son's remittances, but I still watch every yuan. This land has to feed my family.
